For every release claim above: engineering pass, merged code, deployed r-number, and real two-device acceptance are distinct statuses; no newer evidence was read to reclassify these historical failures as fixed.
Preserving known-good live shell, storage keys and rollback semantics made v1.3 safer; feature growth during recovery introduced avoidable acceptance ambiguity.
Source-of-truth handoffs need exact releases, SHAs, fail evidence, next steps and exclusions; broad claims that 'everything is finished' are inadequate without repeatable proof.
Identity is a data semantics problem, not just a UI name problem; display-name unification and fresh profile IDs both have failure cases.
Chromebook/iPhone shell caches can differ even when production is current; display app runtime and pair fingerprint before diagnosing server-side pairing.
A single current-file locator with status and exact next work reduced stale relay/context loops; do not maintain competing handoff authorities.
Deliver actual artifacts and an indexed registry; visual-direction prose without files or integration notes failed the owner's acceptance expectations.

Using Chromebook for Showdown Visual and iPhone for senior product acceptance is workable only when branch responsibilities and handoffs remain explicit; those work roles are not necessarily the in-game manager identity.
A 15-minute transfer challenge plus setup can outlast private-session TTL; foreground/background timers, authentication freshness and reconnect authority must be tested together.
Green deterministic tests cannot substitute for real two-device end-to-end acceptance; always label 'automation green' separately from 'physical pass'.
Separate reviewer lane can catch process defects such as stale SHAs and test-coverage gaps that a code patch alone misses; send findings through lead-controlled integration.
Dividing roles helps: lead defines product truth and acceptance, independent visual worker produces candidates, reviewer checks DOM/product/asset constraints and reproducible handoff.
A superficially tidy dashboard can be completely wrong for a cinematic game product; character staging, lighting, hierarchy and phone composition must be reviewed as a coherent scene.

One targeted edit per ticket with locked faces/hands and original pixels elsewhere is safer than repeatedly generating whole scenes; review crop, anatomy, logos, text and likeness after each revision.
The Journey research yielded shared-operations-room / decision-desk staging: contact light, eyelines and environmental continuity prevent a floating UI between portraits.
Different screen types need different primitives: Transfer War uses bespoke cinematic plates, while Home may use geometric FIFA-style tiles and supporting screens conventional panels.
Factory workers are more reliable with numbered bounded jobs, dependencies, one decision, step-wise commits, status file last and no mid-job asks to the owner.
GitHub connector can read and commit text directly; write-guard refusals require stopping and resuming from latest saved status, not retrying via alternate writes.

Claude/Opus lead, Sol reviewer/worker, Astra/other specialist roles and independent red-team passes can improve coverage, but orchestration overhead and source-backed evaluation matter more than headcount or model branding.
